ballots.title: Who should be next in the Pro Football Hall of Fame?
ballots.note: Former Steelers who are eligible and not yet in Canton (checked against the Class of 2026).

candidates.name: Hines Ward
candidates.text: Team leader in catches, receiving yards and TD catches; Super Bowl XL MVP. He has been a Hall of Fame semifinalist 10 times, most recently for the Class of 2026.

candidates.name: James Harrison
candidates.text: 2008 Defensive Player of the Year and the team’s career sack leader. He has been a semifinalist before but did not advance for 2026.

candidates.name: Ben Roethlisberger
candidates.text: Won two Super Bowls and holds the team’s passing records. He played his last season in 2021, so he is first eligible for the Class of 2027 (voting this winter).

candidates.name: L.C. Greenwood
candidates.text: Six Pro Bowls on the Steel Curtain and a Super Bowl force. He was a modern-era finalist six times and is now a Seniors candidate.

candidates.name: Maurkice Pouncey
candidates.text: Nine Pro Bowls. He became eligible in 2026 and advanced in voting, but did not make the semifinals.

candidates.name: Gary Anderson
candidates.text: Kicked 13 seasons in Pittsburgh and retired as the NFL’s all-time leading scorer. He was nominated for the Class of 2025.

candidates.name: Andy Russell
candidates.text: Seven Pro Bowls and a starter on the first two Super Bowl winners. Seniors candidate.

candidates.name: Greg Lloyd
candidates.text: Five Pro Bowls and the enforcer of the Blitzburgh defenses.

candidates.name: Carnell Lake
candidates.text: Five Pro Bowls at two positions.

candidates.name: Joey Porter Sr.
candidates.text: Three Pro Bowls with Pittsburgh and a Super Bowl XL starter.

candidates.name: Casey Hampton
candidates.text: Five Pro Bowls as the anchor of two championship defenses.

candidates.name: Heath Miller
candidates.text: Two Pro Bowls and the team’s career leader in catches by a tight end.

candidates.name: Kevin Colbert
candidates.text: Built two Super Bowl champions. He would be considered in the contributor category.

candidates.name: Art Rooney Jr.
candidates.text: Ran the scouting department behind the 1970s drafts, including the 1974 class. Contributor category.

ballots.title: Who should be next in the Steelers Hall of Honor?
ballots.note: Former Steelers not yet inducted, checked against the official roster through the Class of 2026. Players must be retired three seasons and have played three seasons here.

candidates.name: Ike Taylor
candidates.text: Shadowed top receivers for 12 seasons and started on two title teams.

candidates.name: Brett Keisel
candidates.text: A seventh-round pick and two-time champion, beloved for his beard and charity “Shear Da Beard” event.

candidates.name: Ryan Clark
candidates.text: Hard-hitting free safety on the Super Bowl XLIII defense. Made the Pro Bowl in 2011.

candidates.name: Kordell Stewart
candidates.text: “Slash” lined up everywhere, then led the 1997 and 2001 teams to the AFC title game.

candidates.name: Gary Anderson
candidates.text: Retired as the NFL’s career scoring leader; scored more points than anyone in team history for decades.

candidates.name: Jeff Hartings
candidates.text: Two Pro Bowls and the starting center for the Super Bowl XL champions.

candidates.name: Deshea Townsend
candidates.text: Versatile defensive back who spent 11 seasons in Pittsburgh and won two rings.

candidates.name: Larry Foote
candidates.text: Hometown-style grinder who started at inside linebacker on two title teams.

candidates.name: Levon Kirkland
candidates.text: Big, mobile inside linebacker who made two Pro Bowls and played in Super Bowl XXX.

candidates.name: David Little
candidates.text: Steady inside linebacker who started for over a decade and made the 1990 Pro Bowl.

candidates.name: Mike Merriweather
candidates.text: Three Pro Bowls in the mid-’80s and one of the top linebackers of his era.

candidates.name: Bryan Hinkle
candidates.text: Started at outside linebacker for 12 seasons through the 1980s and early ’90s.

candidates.name: Ernie Holmes
candidates.text: “Fats” was the fourth starter on the Steel Curtain line and won two rings.

candidates.name: Glen Edwards
candidates.text: Hard-hitting free safety and two-time Pro Bowler on the first two Super Bowl champions.

candidates.name: Bennie Cunningham
candidates.text: First-round tight end who played 10 seasons and won two rings.

candidates.name: Frank Pollard
candidates.text: Tough, reliable back who carried a big share of the load through the 1980s.

candidates.name: Barry Foster
candidates.text: Set the team’s single-season rushing record with 1,690 yards in 1992.

candidates.name: Yancey Thigpen
candidates.text: Two Pro Bowls and a 1,398-yard season in 1997.

candidates.name: Ramon Foster
candidates.text: Undrafted guard who started for most of a decade on a top line.

candidates.name: Jeff Reed
candidates.text: Kicked in two Super Bowl wins, including a field goal in Super Bowl XLIII.

candidates.name: Antwaan Randle El
candidates.text: Threw the TD pass to Hines Ward on a trick play in Super Bowl XL.

candidates.name: Justin Strzelczyk
candidates.text: Versatile lineman who started at tackle and guard, including in Super Bowl XXX.
